Is The NanoCard Bitcoins Killer App?
A slightly improved version of existing bitcoin debit cards does not sound like a killer app.

I think it may be more than a slight improvement. What caught my eye was their saying your funds would be directly debited from your bitcoin balance and that this balance was completely in your control. So not only is it, as far as i can tell, a trust-less decentralized exchange, its also a trust-less wallet and you can pull from it with a MasterCard. That to me is a significant difference.

“New security measures will provide the technology that will enable us to become an exchange, Bitcoin wallet and vault, all in one. You won’t have to worry about our exchange being hacked or whether it is honest or solvent. Everything about our new accounts will be an open book, and you will control the keys to your own funds, even while they are on our exchange.” – CCEDK CEO Ronny Boesing told DigitalMoneyTimes.

Is this an online wallet that happens to have a debit card frontend? I am interested in the internal bitcoin management, not the end-user experience.

[A bit cynical but I am trying to understand without having to read all the advertisement, I am honestly curious about it, not judging yet]

Here's more information from a Forbes article out today:

http://www.forbes.com/sites/rogeraitken/2015/07/16/is-the-nanocard-bitcoins-killer-app-can-it-transform-the-global-remittance-market/2/

I was kinda wondering what the point of pegging to fiat was. Because if you purchase $1000 worth of BTC as an investment, but then peg it to remove volatility then why not just buy the BTC only when you need it for spending online? I suppose if you think a banking collapse is imminent then you might prefer to hold the pegged crypto at least.

I got thinking that maybe this would be very convenient though for people already holding BTC. You'd deposit it and then spend through debit card. If using multi-sig, etc. then you're assured that you have control of your coins at all times. No more moving funds from paper wallets to exchange and then fiat back to bank account. Guess it all depends on the security.
